title: logical decoding with test_decoding: the WAL turned back into row changes
setup:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id int PRIMARY KEY, owner text NOT NULL, balance numeric(12,2) NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO accounts VALUES (1, 'alice', 100.00), (2, 'bob', 100.00);

steps.note: a logical slot with the test_decoding plugin. from here on, the server keeps every change this slot hasn't consumed.
a transfer: two updates in one transaction.

steps.sql:
INSERT INTO accounts VALUES (3, 'carol', 50.00);
DELETE FROM accounts WHERE id = 2
steps.note: a new account, and a closed one.

steps.sql: SELECT data FROM pg_logical_slot_get_changes('cdc', NULL, NULL)
steps.note: reading the slot: every committed change since it was created, in commit order, as rows.

data: table public.accounts: UPDATE: id[integer]:1 owner[text]:'alice' balance[numeric]:75.00
table public.accounts: UPDATE: id[integer]:2 owner[text]:'bob' balance[numeric]:125.00
table public.accounts: INSERT: id[integer]:3 owner[text]:'carol' balance[numeric]:50.00

steps.sql: SELECT count(*) AS changes FROM pg_logical_slot_get_changes('cdc', NULL, NULL)
steps.note: read it again: nothing. get_changes consumed them; the slot's position moved past them.
replica identity full: the WAL now carries the whole old row on UPDATE and DELETE, not just the key.

steps.sql: SELECT data FROM pg_logical_slot_get_changes('cdc', NULL, NULL)
steps.note: the same kind of changes, now with old-key showing every column of the row before.

data: table public.accounts: UPDATE: old-key: id[integer]:1 owner[text]:'alice' balance[numeric]:75.00 new-tuple: id[integer]:1 owner[text]:'alice' balance[numeric]:76.00
table public.accounts: DELETE: id[integer]:3 owner[text]:'carol' balance[numeric]:50.00

steps.sql: SELECT count(*) AS changes FROM pg_logical_slot_peek_changes('cdc', NULL, NULL)
steps.note: it never shows up: decoding only emits committed transactions.

steps.sql:
SELECT slot_name FROM pg_create_logical_replication_slot('cdc_ha', 'pgoutput', failover => true);
SELECT slot_name, plugin, slot_type, failover FROM pg_replication_slots ORDER BY slot_name
steps.note: a failover slot (postgres 17+): marked so a standby can keep a synced copy and take over the stream.
